US stocks inch up even as election, AI risks weigh on outlook
article:
(Nov 3): US stocks were higher after the market opened as Americans headed to the polls on Election Day, with control of both chambers of Congress at stake and investors weighing mounting risks to the artificial intelligence (AI) trade.

The S&P 500 Index gained 0.2% while the Nasdaq 100 advanced 0.6% as of 9.33am in New York, clawing back earlier losses. Technology shares attempted a rebound a day after entering a correction.

The election adds another layer of uncertainty to an already fragile market backdrop. Polymarket is pricing roughly a 95% probability of Democrats taking the House of Representatives and about a 77% chance of a Senate victory, pointing to a potential sweep of both chambers. The divergence between opinion polls and prediction-market expectations has drawn fresh attention as investors position for the outcome.

History, however, has generally favoured stocks following midterm elections. Large-cap equities have gained about 15% on a market-cap-weighted basis and 16% on an equal-weighted basis in the six months after midterms since 1982, according to Morgan Stanley. Both measures have advanced roughly 22% over the subsequent year.

“For all the prognostications and reactions to tonight’s results, here’s the key stat to remember: While past performance doesn’t guarantee future results, since 1950, so 76 years, the S&P 500 has never been lower 12 months after a midterm election, and that is the most notable point of all for clients,” said Tom Essaye, founder of The Sevens Report.

To UBS Securities, US stocks may be poised for a year-end rebound as favourable seasonality and low hedge fund positioning set the stage for a potential rally after the midterm elections.

See also: US stock rotation hits AI winners on spending worries

“Hyperscaler earnings clearly did not provide the all-clear investors were hoping for, but getting through the election could be the catalyst that unlocks a year-end squeeze,” Davide Montoni, Americas head of institutional equity derivatives and QIS sales at UBS Securities, wrote in a note to clients.

Still, investor positioning suggests caution is building. Investors added a further US$9.6 billion ($12.3 billion) in net new short positions in S&P 500 futures last week, bringing overall positioning close to neutral, according to Citigroup strategists. Nasdaq futures saw a similar trend. Positioning in Russell 2000 futures improved, driven by short-covering and suggesting investors have become less bearish on US small-cap stocks, Citi strategists led by David Chew said.

Concerns about the sustainability of AI spending are adding to the unease. As tech heavyweights increasingly turn to bond markets to finance their AI investments, some of the world’s largest asset managers are warning that the boom risks are developing into a bubble. Pacific Investment Management Co chief executive officer Emmanuel Roman and Bain Capital chair John Connaughton are among investors flagging the possibility of an eventual downturn following the sector’s rapid expansion, even as Wall Street executives continue to tout its long-term potential.

See also: Tech stocks slide as Alphabet’s record plunge revives AI fears

In single stocks, Apple Inc added to the pressure after its latest quarterly results disappointed on several key metrics, including revenue in China. Yum! Brands Inc shares rose as RBC says Taco Bell’s third quarter comparable sales drop of 4% is better than the buyside feared. Palantir Technologies Inc shares tumbled after the software company issued a quarterly outlook that pointed to a potential slowdown in sales growth.

The earnings backdrop has remained relatively resilient. Companies representing about 70% of the S&P 500’s market capitalisation have reported third-quarter results, with 84% beating earnings estimates and 13% missing expectations.
• AI-linked stocks are rebounding after three days of declines. Neocloud firms including CoreWeave and Nebius and chipmaker Intel all gained after the market opened.
• Defence stocks could face another headwind from increased Democratic influence as elections could reset the Pentagon’s fiscal 2027 budget towards 2026 levels and flatten spending growth through 2028.
• Energy stocks fell after oil sharply dropped more than 1.7% premarket. Oil-sensitive sectors including travel and cruises are in focus.

title: Binance loses market share to crypto exchange rivals after hack
article:
(Nov 3): Binance may have digested the largest ever crypto hack with relative ease, but not without ceding some of its dominance in digital-asset trading to rivals.

The exchange’s share of crypto trading fell to its lowest level in at least 12 weeks as platforms including OKX gained ground in the aftermath of last week’s US$6.3 billion ($8.1 billion) hack, according to data from Kaiko, an analytics firm.

Over the past seven days, Binance accounted for about 42% of the spot trading volume on the market’s top-10 platforms, down from around 48% prior to the hack and from roughly 51% in mid-August. Coinbase, OKX and Kraken all increased their share in that time.

Binance suspended withdrawals after an Oct 29 cyber-theft that the US Federal Bureau of Investigation has attributed to North Korean hackers — a charge the country denies. Elliptic, the blockchain analytics firm, said its analysis “supports the FBI’s attribution specifically to the North Korean state-linked group TraderTraitor”.

As of Monday, Binance held US$157 billion in assets, a spokesperson said at the time, citing internal estimates that factor in the impact of hack, subsequent withdrawals and price fluctuations. The company had earlier said it had US$171 billion in assets, in an X post on Sunday.

See also: North Korea’s hackers supercharge crypto heists with AI skills

The platform restored withdrawals on Sunday. Customers have since pulled a net US$5.6 billion, about 3.5% of Binance’s total assets, according to a spokesperson.

Now the immediate pressure from the hack appears to be easing. “By around 3:00 UTC on Nov 3, hourly deposits began exceeding hourly withdrawals, reflecting improving user activity and a normalisation of flows,” the spokesperson said.

Fuelled by higher spot trading volume, OKX’s market share rose to about 14% in the past seven days, up from about 11% the prior week, while Coinbase’s grew to 9.6% from about 9%, the Kaiko data show.
